answer: Agents must lock a scarce bond in a vault before submitting work; peers release it only after verifying useful contributions over time. A lantern-style audit checks claims and slashes bonds for fake identities or copied work. An attacker can make many accounts, but must fund each bond and risk losing it, so a sybil swarm ties up real capital. Reputation builds slowly, and an ember of trust earned by one account cannot simply be copied to others.
